source.title: Toward Moderate Overparameterization: Global Convergence Guarantees for Training Shallow Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full text supplied. The paper text is titled “Towards moderate overparameterization” and matches the identified study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how shallow networks trained by gradient methods fit arbitrary labels as model size varies, using randomly generated regression data and random labels. It does not test generalization on natural labels or held-out examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-fit results relevant to memorization capacity. Its CIFAR-10 label-shuffling discussion cites prior work and is not a result of this study; the experiments use random inputs and random regression labels, not natural data or held-out test error.
record.test_reason: The study measures optimization and interpolation of synthetic regression labels, not coexistence of memorization and held-out generalization (V1), or test error as width increases (V2). It explicitly leaves generalization to future work. Its discussion of shuffled CIFAR-10 labels reports prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish sufficient overparameterization conditions for convergence to interpolating solutions near initialization, and empirically observe random-label fitting near kd = n. The theoretical sufficient conditions are stronger than that empirical threshold. They explicitly leave the relationship between optimization and generalization for future research.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies one-hidden-layer networks with random inputs and random real-valued labels, measuring training fit as width and input dimension vary. It does not reproduce the natural-label and held-out evaluation used in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation (softplus versus ReLU), training-set size (n = 100 versus n = 200), and the product kd relative to n affect the reported training-fit success region.

fits_no_version.finding: For softplus and ReLU networks on synthetic inputs and Gaussian regression labels, fitting success transitions near kd = n, with a tighter transition at n = 200 than n = 100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent can fit random regression labels in shallow networks with only modest parameter-count overparameterization.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory
record.problems: Experiments use randomly generated inputs and real-valued random labels rather than natural data; they report training fit only. The empirical probability averages 10 realizations per (k, d) pair, with no error bars stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results for claim versions were reported. The CIFAR-10 random-label example in Section 4 is cited prior work, not an experiment in this paper.

untested.parts: Natural-label performance and held-out performance under natural and random labels using the same architectures and recipes; synthetic random-label interpolation alone does not test coexistence.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected row states concern their inability to measure any listed claim version; they do not dispute the observed training-fit results. Section 3's qualitative statement about generalization of random-feature least-norm solutions supplies no result testing a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper discusses random-label fitting but does not test the same architectures and recipes on natural labels, nor report held-out accuracy on natural or random labels.
The paper varies hidden width and input dimension for random-label training success, but does not test test error on natural labels or networks widened beyond an interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
No batch-size comparison or held-out performance result.
No removal of memorized examples or test-accuracy measurement.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer neural network, softplus activation
rows.size_stated: n = 100; k and d varied between 0 to 25
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden units k and input dimension d; trained by gradient descent on random regression labels and measured fitting success.

conditions.value: n = 100; inputs drawn i.i.d. from unit sphere; labels i.i.d. standard normal
15000 or until relative Euclidean error falls below 2.5 × 10−3

rows.measure: Empirical probability of successful training fit, where success is relative loss less than 2.5 × 10−3; averaged 10 independent realizations per (k, d) pair.
rows.value: Success region is tightly surrounded by the n = kd curve; neural nets can overfit as soon as the problem is slightly overparameterized.
rows.uncertainty: 10 independent realizations for each (k, d) pair; no error bar stated.
rows.note: Training-fit probability on randomly generated data and labels; not a held-out generalization result.
rows.check: Training-fit success on synthetic regression data cannot establish V1's coexistence claim. The fitting result is reported correctly, but the output weights are fixed at their theorem-specified values; only input-to-hidden weights are trained.
